correctness.rationale: For Q>=r+2, each outer vertex has degree r<Q-1 and cannot ever be forced; therefore every successful seed fully colours all rm outer vertices. If the hub is coloured this is a proper complete Q-colouring, counted by Q ((Q-1)_r)^m. If it is blank, its Q-1 neighbour colours must cover exactly Q-1 distinct labels; choosing the unique absent label and inclusion-exclusion over colours not used in m ordered r-injections gives Q S_{r,m}(Q-1). The cover count is positive exactly for r<=Q-1<=rm, proving the two-step palette threshold and all coefficients. The probability formula applies the independent p/s weighting. For fixed r and m r/t-log t ->c, fixed-order Bonferroni sums tend to alternating partial sums of exp(-exp(-c)), which squeeze to that limit. A direct independent graph-state verifier exhaustively compared every coefficient in eight small parameter instances; this corroborates but does not establish universal truth.

value.rationale: The theorem supplies the full formerly absent nonchromatic palette axis Q>=r+2 for a natural infinite clique-block graph family and isolates a graph-local structural mechanism: one extra colour makes every outer vertex permanently unforceable. This yields a sharp distinct two-stage threshold in optimal seed count, exact multiplicities, a two-coefficient probability formula for every integer r,m,Q, and a natural colour-coverage transition. It is a complete structural classification for an infinite parameter range, not merely a numerical experiment, a renaming, or a reformulation of the earlier Q=r+1 expression. The Bonferroni limit is supplementary classical methodology, not the novelty premise.
